title: datacurve-ai/deep-swe — Measuring frontier coding agents on original, long-horizon engineering tasks
content:
DeepSWE is a benchmark for measuring frontier coding agents on original, long-horizon software engineering tasks drawn from active open-source repositories. The benchmark includes 113 tasks across TypeScript, Go, Python, JavaScript, and Rust, with isolated environments and program-based verifiers.
DeepSWE tasks use the Harbor task format:
task.toml         Metadata (repo, base commit, language, image, limits)
instruction.md    The prompt the agent sees
environment/      Dockerfile reproducing the prebuilt image
tests/            Verifier entry point, held-out tests, and grader config
solution/         Reference solution (held out from the agent)
The verifier exercises the behavior the prompt describes. It accepts any solution whose observable behavior is correct, regardless of internal symbol names or structure.
The reference patch in solution/ is never used at grading time; it exists so reviewers can spot-check correctness offline.
Since v1.1, grading uses Harbor's separate verifier environment, requiring Pier newer than 0.3.0. The agent works in an isolated environment and commits its work upon completion. A [[verifier.collect]] hook in each task.toml then extracts these commits as a patch, which is applied and graded in a pristine container.
The verifier produces the following outputs for each run:
verifier/
    reward.json      Structured scores (binary reward + pass fractions)
    ctrf.json        Machine-readable test report with failure messages
    test-stdout.txt  Raw suite output and a list of failure reasons
    run.log          Raw stdout/stderr captured during the run
    reports/         Framework-native report/log files from the grader
Use Pier to run the benchmark:
git clone https://github.com/datacurve-ai/deep-swe
uv tool install datacurve-pier
# Claude Opus 4.8
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=...
pier run -p deep-swe/tasks --agent mini-swe-agent --model anthropic/claude-opus-4-8
# GPT-5.5
export OPENAI_API_KEY=...
pier run -p deep-swe/tasks --agent mini-swe-agent --model openai/gpt-5.5
Pier is a Harbor-compatible framework for sandboxed coding-agent evals. It began as a fork of Harbor to support CLI agents in air-gapped tasks: Harbor blocks all outbound traffic in allow_internet = false tasks, including dependency installs and LLM API calls. Pier adds per-agent network allowlists, giving agents only the network access they need while keeping the task environment isolated.
Pier also adds more complete trajectory metadata, a better trajectory viewer, and pier critique run for analyzing agent trajectories. All leaderboard scores were produced with Pier running mini-swe-agent on Modal.
mini-swe-agent is model-agnostic. Pier also drives claude-code, codex, gemini-cli, and opencode directly. Pass --env modal to run in parallel sandboxes on Modal.
Deterministic random subset of the 113-task corpus:
pier run -p deep-swe/tasks --agent mini-swe-agent --n-tasks 10 --sample-seed 0
Single task:
pier run -p deep-swe/tasks/<task-id> --agent mini-swe-agent

report.summary: DeepSWE is a benchmark of 113 original, long-horizon engineering tasks from active open-source repositories to evaluate frontier coding agents.
report.background: Most coding-agent benchmarks, like SWE-bench, measure whether an agent can fix real bugs in existing repositories using patch-matching against human PRs. DeepSWE flips the focus: instead of bug-fixing known issues, it tests original, long-horizon engineering tasks written from scratch and drawn from active open-source projects. The 113 tasks span TypeScript, Go, Python, JavaScript, and Rust, and each task runs in an isolated Docker environment with a program-based verifier that checks observable behavior, not internals. This means agents must implement features or refactor code from a prompt, then produce commits that pass held-out tests. The benchmark adopts Harbor's task format (task.toml, instruction.md, environment/, tests/, solution/). Since v1.1, it also relies on Pier, a Harbor-compatible runner for CLI coding agents in sandboxed, network-allowlisted environments.
key_points: DeepSWE contains 113 benchmark tasks across TypeScript, Go, Python, JavaScript, and Rust. Unlike benchmarks that recycle real GitHub issues, these are original, long-horizon engineering assignments built from active open-source repositories, so agents cannot train on existing solutions or known issue fixes.

Grading is behavior-based, not patch-based. A program verifier exercises what the instruction describes and accepts any solution with correct observable behavior, regardless of internal symbols, names, or code structure. The reference patch exists only for offline human review and is never used at grading time.

DeepSWE is built on Harbor's task format and run with Pier, a Harbor-compatible framework for coding-agent evals. Each agent works in an isolated container, commits its work, and a verifier-collect hook extracts that commit as a patch, which is then applied and tested in a pristine verifier environment.

The runner reports structured results: reward.json contains binary reward and pass fractions; ctrf.json gives a machine-readable test report; test-stdout.txt shows raw output and failure reasons; run.log captures full logs. This makes failures auditable and reproducible.

DeepSWE is model- and agent-agnostic. Pier drives mini-swe-agent, claude-code, codex, gemini-cli, and opencode, and supports parallel execution on Modal. It also allows deterministic random subsets via --n-tasks and --sample-seed for cheaper or partial evaluation.
report.impact: DeepSWE raises the bar for coding-agent evaluation by focusing on original work rather than patch-matching known issues. That makes scores harder to game through memorization and more meaningful for real engineering capability. For AI developers, it provides a transparent workflow with reproducible isolated environments and structured outputs, letting them preflight new models or agent scaffolds before shipping. Model labs and tool vendors can use the benchmark to identify weaknesses in long-horizon planning, multi-file edits, or specific languages. For regular users, benchmarks like this signal which agents can genuinely handle multi-step engineering requests rather than only tutorial-level snippets. It also pushes ecosystem innovation: improved runners such as Pier, better task formats such as Harbor, and a community standard for sealed, behavioral testing of agents.
report.tools: Watch or use: datacurve-ai/deep-swe on GitHub; Pier (datacurve-pier) for running benchmarks; Harbor as the underlying task-format and eval scaffold; mini-swe-agent as the reference agent. Install with uv tool install datacurve-pier and run pier run -p deep-swe/tasks to reproduce leaderboard scores.
